papers.title_in_file: Compositional Quantum Heuristics for Max-Clique Detection
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, setup, tasks and models, training dynamics, generalisation, recursive models, clique-number models, conclusion. Definitions, propositions and appendices skimmed or not read.
papers.what_it_is: Simulated study of symmetry-equivariant parameterised quantum circuits for finding maximum cliques, with a recursive hybrid heuristic.

assertions.value: The authors report that their symmetry-based quantum graph models show larger training gradients than non-symmetric models and generalise to larger, more complex problem instances.
quotes: The models we construct exhibit superior training gradients through symmetry-induced bias, and our experiments demonstrate that the trained models generalise to larger, more complex problem instances.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on simulated max-clique tasks.
assertions.reader_inference: The result is shown on simulated Erdos-Renyi graphs only; no hardware run is described.

assertions.value: The authors state that they design quantum graph neural network models for detecting maximally sized cliques in simple graphs.
quotes: In this work we design quantum graph neural network models for detecting maximally sized cliques in simple graphs
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope in the introduction, p.3.

assertions.value: The authors report that the deeper non-equivariant model exhibits the steepest decline and achieves no better than the random guessing baseline over unseen graph sizes.
quotes: The 20 layer AsymKA model exhibits the steepest decline, achieving no better than the random guessing baseline over unseen graph sizes.
assertions.certainty_reason: One experiment within one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the recursive quantum heuristic is competitive with classical baselines, and that it only surpasses the upper baseline where the inner model has a high distribution accuracy.
quotes: Encouragingly, we also find that the quantum heuristic is competitive relative to classical baselines
although it only surpasses the upper baseline in the range where the inner
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study; the baselines are simple classical heuristics.
assertions.reader_inference: The classical baselines named are uniform and degree-proportional node choice, which are weak heuristics.

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, Theorem 1 and its discussion, conclusions. Appendix proofs not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: Theory paper proposing a quantum agent-environment framework and showing quantum speedups for reinforcement learning in restricted environments.

assertions.value: The paper states that its constructed quantum reinforcement learning agents outperform their classical counterparts quadratically in terms of learning efficiency, or exponentially in performance over limited periods.
quotes: which outperform their classical counterparts quadratically in terms of learning efficiency, or even exponentially in performance over limited periods.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1 and the construction following it, main text; derived, not run.
assertions.reader_inference: Result holds in oracular, restricted environments.

assertions.value: The paper states that, in the restricted settings of deterministic epochal environments, the learning efficiency of all learning agents can generically be improved, provided the environments are luck-favoring for those agents.
quotes: This Theorem states that, in the restricted settings of determinisic epochal environments, it is possible to generically improve the learning efficiency of all learning agents, provided the environments are luck-favoring for those agents.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the scope of Theorem 1 in the text following the theorem.

assertions.value: The paper states that the theorem applies to a deterministic, strictly epochal environment and is not quantitative, due to the generality of the definition of luck-favoring settings.
quotes: Let E be a deterministic, strictly epochal environment.
The statement of Theorem 1 is not quantitative, due to the generality of the definition of luck-favoring settings.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state this limit in the main text at Theorem 1.
assertions.reader_inference: The advantage needs an oracular environment variant, not a standard environment.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum routing in planar graph using perfect state transfer
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, preliminaries, conclusion. Construction sections and examples skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: Theory paper on routing quantum states in planar spin networks using perfect state transfer with switchable couplings.

assertions.value: The authors state that they give multiple examples of planar graphs supporting quantum routing where classical routing is not possible.
quotes: We elaborate multiple examples of planar graphs supporting quantum routing where classical routing is not possible.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' claim backed by worked examples in the paper, not by an experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that their examples show that quantum routing is more efficient than its classical counterparts.
quotes: Our examples show that quantum routing is more efficient than their classical counterparts.
assertions.certainty_reason: Claim in the conclusion based on constructed examples.

assertions.value: The authors state that the performance of multiple perfect state transfer needs control over the interactions, which could be experimentally challenging.
quotes: Performance of multiple PST needs control over the interactions. This could be experimentally challenging.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state the limit in the conclusion, p.7.

assertions.value: The authors state that they assume all possible coupling strengths are equal, which makes the graph a simple graph.
quotes: Here, we assume that all possible coupling strength are equal to 1, which makes G a simple graph.
assertions.certainty_reason: Setup statement in section 2.

papers.title_in_file: Investigation of D-Wave quantum annealing for training Restricted Boltzmann Machines and mitigating catastrophic forgetting
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, conclusion. Methods and results sections skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: Experimental study of hybrid D-Wave and classical sampling for training RBMs and of generative replay for catastrophic forgetting.

assertions.value: The authors report that the hybrid sampling approach failed to achieve any substantial improvement in training quality compared to the regular contrastive divergence training.
quotes: The approach failed to achieve any substantial improvement in the training quality compared to the regular
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical negative result from one study on D-Wave hardware.

assertions.value: The authors report that classification performance of the hybrid training and of the D-Wave-seeded training was somewhat worse than standard training with Gibbs sampling, while log-likelihood results were comparable.
quotes: the classification performance of the hybrid training, as well as the training utilizing only seeds produced by the D-Wave, were somewhat worse than
while the results for the log-likelihood were comparable between the three sampling methods.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that D-Wave-based mitigation of catastrophic forgetting performed similarly to classical MCMC mitigation, and that D-Wave generates patterns much faster than the classical method.
quotes: The performance of the D-Wave-based mitigation of the CF was similar to that of the mitigation utilizing classical MCMC.

assertions.value: The authors state that the reasons for the inferiority of the approaches using the annealer are tentatively attributed to less-than-perfect embedding of the RBM into the annealer.
quotes: is tentatively attributed to the less-than-perfect embedding

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks for Jet Images Classification
papers.version_note: File is the v3 (September 2025) of the arXiv paper; matches the record title.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, conclusion and outlook. Methods and results sections skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: Simulated study comparing quantum convolutional neural networks with classical CNNs on top-quark jet images.

assertions.value: The authors report that the quantum convolutional network, in the absence of noise, performs better than the corresponding classical CNN for most choices of data encoding, batch size, loss function and convolutional block.
quotes: the QCNN, in the absence of noise, performs better than the corresponding CNN model for most choices of data encoding, batch-size, loss function, and convolutional block involved.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study, on a classical noiseless simulator.

assertions.value: The authors state that they only performed noiseless simulation and that noise would spoil the quantum network performance unless it can be tamed.
quotes: Besides, we only performed the noiseless simulation and the effects from noise would spoil the QCNN performance unless we can tame them.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state this limit in the conclusion.

assertions.value: The authors state that the system was relatively simple, and that they do not claim their model outperforms all the existing models.
quotes: it is important to emphasize that the system we studied here was relatively simple, both in QCNN and CNN.
we are not claiming that our model outperforms all the existing models
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state these limits in the conclusion.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum convolutional network has been indicated to be classically simulable for the classification of classical data.
quotes: As QCNN has been indicated to be classically simulable [21] for the classification of classical data
assertions.certainty_reason: Result attributed to another work.

papers.title_in_file: Graph Representation Learning for Parameter Transferability in Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, parts of the results (sections 5.3 to 5.5), conclusion.
papers.what_it_is: Simulation study using graph embeddings to pick donor graphs whose optimal QAOA parameters transfer to MaxCut targets.

assertions.value: The authors report that the technique reduces the iterations required for parameter optimization, obtaining an approximate solution to the target problem with an order of magnitude speedup.
quotes: we effectively reduce the number of iterations required for parameter optimization, obtaining an approximate solution to the target problem with an order of magnitude speedup.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from simulations on small graphs in one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that among five whole graph embedding algorithms, Graph2Vec had the best overall performance for finding donor graphs.
quotes: Among the set of five whole graph embedding algorithms, the Graph2Vec algorithm had the best overall performance
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical comparison in one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that, given noise in modern quantum processors, their results demonstrate that parameters obtained from graph embeddings retain their utility.
quotes: Given the noise inherent in modern quantum processors, our results demonstrate that parameters obtained from graph embeddings retain their utility.
assertions.certainty_reason: Noisy-simulator result (mock backends) in one study, not hardware.
assertions.reader_inference: The noise evidence is from simulated mock backends, not real hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that, as of writing, there are no other well-studied graph features that predict good QAOA parameter transferability between two MaxCut instances.
quotes: As of the writing of this article, there are no other well-studied graph features that predict good QAOA parameter transferability between two MaxCut instances.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author statement about the state of the field.

assertions.value: The authors state that they focus on quantum gate computing and on its potential and limitations for machine learning tasks on classical data.
quotes: we focus on quantum gate computing, and our aim is to deepen the understanding of its potential and limitations for machine learning tasks on classical data
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state the survey scope in the introduction.

assertions.value: The authors state that comprehensive studies that systematically examine the contributions of the quantum components in hybrid models to their gains are still lacking.
quotes: However, comprehensive studies that systematically examine the contributions of the quantum components in the hybrid models to these gains are still lacking.
assertions.certainty_reason: Survey authors' assessment of the field.

assertions.value: The authors state that a systematic understanding of how different quantum gates and circuit configurations affect learning capacity is still lacking.
quotes: A systematic understanding of how different quantum gates and circuit configurations affect learning capacity is still lacking.
assertions.certainty_reason: Survey authors' assessment of the field.

assertions.value: The authors report that a cited study found quantum machine learning models have a strong ability to memorize data.
quotes: the empirical results indicate QML models have a strong ability to memorize data.
assertions.certainty_reason: Result attributed to Gil et al., cited in the survey.

papers.title_in_file: Classification with Quantum Neural Networks on Near Term Processors
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction and setup, digit-classification section (in part), conclusions and outlook. Boolean-function construction sections skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: Proposal of a quantum neural network for binary classification, with classical simulation on downsampled handwritten digits.

assertions.value: The authors state that, through classical simulation, parameters can be found that allow the quantum neural network to learn to correctly distinguish two handwritten digit data sets.
quotes: We show through classical simulation that parameters can be found that allow the QNN to learn to correctly distinguish the two data sets.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulation study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the data set could easily be classified by a classical network, that working at a fixed low number of bits precludes any discussion of scaling, and that the work is exploratory.
quotes: Admittedly the data set could easily be classified by a classical network.
precludes any discussion of scaling. But our work is exploratory
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state these limits in the digit section.

assertions.value: The authors state that they ran a classical computer as a simulator, without access yet to an actual error-free quantum computer, and that this served as a proof of principle.
quotes: we ran a classical computer as a simulator of a quantum device.
This exercise served as a proof of principle that our quantum methodology could be used to classify real world data.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own framing; proof of principle that was run in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors state that for certain label functions the circuit is exponentially long.
quotes: For certain label functions the circuit is exponentially long.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the abstract as a property of their Boolean-function construction.
